entrypoint.normalEvaluation: Pure standard-library evaluation; no callback, file/network operation or automatic clock read.

envelope.fixtureId: Opaque nonempty ASCII fixture label, at most 96 characters; does not attest to a real artifact.

namespace.sessionId: Opaque stable session token, at most 96 ASCII characters; a date in a fixture label is not authenticated by the module.
namespace.rawSymbol: Explicit exact symbol token, at most 32 ASCII characters; no continuous-contract mapping, expiry guessing or real definition lookup.

source.artifactId: Explicit synthetic artifact token; not inferred from a path, not read or authenticated.

record.namespace: Must exactly equal the fixture envelope namespace.
record.mdTradeEntryId: integer 1..4294967295; trade-group reference only, never unique source-report identity.
record.price: signed integer -9223372036854775808..9223372036854775806, in 1/priceScale units; 9223372036854775807 refused. No floating-point price conversion.
record.quantity: integer 1..4294967294 contracts; no bool, float, zero, negative, string or maximum-u32 sentinel.

aggressorSide.corrections: CHANGE and DELETE require raw code 0. Original code and interpretation are preserved; correction code never overwrites them.

record.eventTimeNs: integer 0..18446744073709551614; original exchange-event clock for NEW, correction's own event clock for an update. May decrease across source-ordered messages.
record.messageTimeNs: integer 0..18446744073709551614; explicitly supplied source-message clock; not auto-derived from event time or sequence.
record.availableTimeNs: integer 0..18446744073709551614; explicitly supplied synthetic consumer-knowledge clock. Vendor receive time alone is not evidence of actual consumer knowledge.
record.sequence: integer 0..4294967295, retained as data only; neither identity nor gap proof.
record.rptSeq: integer 0..4294967295, retained as data only; never a prior-trade reference.
record.eventComplete: Must be literal true as a fixture assertion. This is not native event-completion validation.

identity.sourceReportId: fixture-report: + SHA-256 of canonical JSON of those three source fields
identity.exactReplay: Same physical tuple and identical canonical decoded record bytes; no extra history, quantity or diagnostics. JSON whitespace/key order is irrelevant; no binary-frame duplicate claim.
identity.conflictingReplay: Same physical tuple with different canonical decoded fields refuses reached-prefix qualification.
identity.positionRules: For each synthetic artifact, previously unseen physical ordinal and byte offset both strictly increase. A reused ordinal or byte offset with a different tuple refuses. Identities are retained, never evicted.
identity.nativeId: Separate from physical identity; repeated native trade-group IDs across distinct NEW rows remain separate active source observations.

actions.NEW: Adds a separately identified source observation and original gross quantity. Repeated native trade-group ID is allowed.
actions.CHANGE: Exactly one active source observation with that native trade-group ID in the fixed namespace; quantity must equal original/current quantity; changes only integer price. Original source, event time, message/knowledge clocks and aggressor remain. Retains correction record and new price/message/knowledge basis.
actions.DELETE: Exactly one active target; current active price and quantity must both match. Removes once and transfers exact quantity into cancelled partition. Exact physical replay is idempotent; any distinct update after deletion must independently qualify and usually has no active target.
actions.ambiguity: Zero or multiple active targets refuses; never disambiguate by price, latest position, RptSeq, sequence or an inferred order identity.
actions.refusal: On any reached semantic error, all authoritative-looking totals become null and active/cancelled result arrays are empty. Full reached history and prefix issues remain; later reached records are not applied.

clocks.cutoffBoundary: Both inclusive messageTimeNs <= message cutoff and availableTimeNs <= knowledge cutoff are required. Stop before first source-ordered row whose trustworthy message OR knowledge clock exceeds its corresponding cutoff.
clocks.sourcePrefixOnly: Observed source-prefix arithmetic, not an event-time watermark, proof that no later source row carries an earlier time, or complete exchange-time reconstruction.
clocks.ordering: Unique reached physical reports require nondecreasing message and knowledge clocks. Exact physical replay is handled before regression checks. Event times may decrease; source records are never resorted.
clocks.chain: Every semantically valid record requires eventTimeNs <= messageTimeNs <= availableTimeNs.
clocks.untrustedClock: A reached row missing a trustworthy message or knowledge clock refuses; it cannot be assumed future. A trustworthy other clock beyond its cutoff can stop before its bad body. A prior trustworthy boundary excludes even a later unclocked malformed tail.
clocks.futureInvariance: With the same admitted fixture metadata and limits, appending out-of-prefix records cannot change earlier snapshot bytes or diagnostics. There is no whole-input hash/count or global late-error flag in a snapshot.
clocks.actualClocks: No clock is synthesized, substituted with wall time, or inferred from source sequences. All clocks in this component are explicitly synthetic assertions.

parsingAndResources.transportAdmission: Whole-input bytes type, JSON syntax/representability, exact synthetic envelope and byte/record caps are evaluated before constructing a ledger. Failure raises InputRefused; it is separate from prefix semantic qualification.
parsingAndResources.futureBodyHandling: Actual parser-detected duplicate objects retain ONLY their original key/value pairs, with no selected-value alias. Parser-origin metadata permits reading unique original source/clock fields for identity/cutoff decisions only. Literal marker objects cannot claim that provenance. Actual duplicate clocks remain untrusted. Reached duplicate objects remain semantically invalid; future excluded body defects cannot alter earlier queries.

__duplicate_json_fields__.pairs: All original key/value pairs, each original value stored once. No duplicate object's selected child values are also retained alongside these pairs.

parsingAndResources.maxTotalQuantity: 9223372036854775807; exact checked integer gross, active and cancelled quantities. Limits may only be lowered.
parsingAndResources.identityCapScope: Reached-prefix semantic refusal, with no identity eviction.
parsingAndResources.recordCapScope: Whole-input transport refusal, including duplicates and future records. An over-cap appended file is a different, unadmitted input; no historical snapshot is issued from it.
parsingAndResources.unparseableJson: A syntactically broken JSON document cannot be safely partitioned into future records; construction refuses rather than emitting a partial ledger.
parsingAndResources.serializedStorageScope: Whole-input total of immutable canonical metadata plus every stored row; Limits.max_serialized_bytes may lower the 8 MiB ceiling. A remaining budget is passed into each encoding operation, not checked only after materialization.
parsingAndResources.serializationAlgorithm: Canonical writer checks remaining bytes before every append. Each escaped string/key chunk is limited to 256 input characters, so a large string is never encoded as one unbounded chunk. Nested duplicate evidence has a linear tree representation.
parsingAndResources.serializationRefusal: SERIALIZED_BYTE_CAP is a resource-admission exception, separate from prefix semantic diagnostics; no partial ledger is returned.
parsingAndResources.canonicalOutputScope: snapshot_bytes also uses the writer's fixed 8 MiB hard ceiling; an oversized serialization raises resource refusal rather than returning truncated JSON. Lowering max_serialized_bytes changes stored-input admission only. snapshot returns its fresh bounded-input-derived dictionary without serializing it.
parsingAndResources.parserOrigin: Only the JSON object-pairs parser can create the private duplicate-object type. Construction captures that provenance in an immutable per-row boolean outside caller JSON. Later original-pair extraction requires this bit; the marker's spelling or shape alone never authenticates clocks or a physical source.
parsingAndResources.literalMarker: A caller-supplied __duplicate_json_fields__ object is ordinary input. Only its real unique top-level message/availability/source fields can be considered. No such raw clocks means reached-prefix refusal. Genuine future top-level clocks may still exclude its malformed body.

output.qualifiedFixtureSample: Only validation/accounting of the reached explicit synthetic sample, not provider or exchange qualification.
output.identityCaution: Observation/report counts are not distinct orders. distinctNativeOrderCount is always null.
output.conservation: grossReportedQuantity == activeQuantity + cancelledQuantity, also separately for BUY/SELL/NO_AGGRESSOR.
output.history: Unique reached decoded physical records in preserved input order, including raw aggressor code, correction's own clocks, action outcome and refusal reason.
output.immutability: Input stored as immutable canonical bytes; every snapshot builds fresh state. Mutating returned nested dictionaries/lists does not change any later query.
output.eligibility: fixtureOnly true, publicConsumerEligible false, completeCmeVolume false, nativeDecoderProven false, atomicCmeEventProven false.
